messages:
kevin: vuln-bot just pushed CVE-2027-4421 for aws-signature-v4-js (transitive via http-proxy). external recon shows probes hitting /v1/public/* endpoints, low volume but consistent since 8:00 UTC. can we prioritize? :eyes:

vuln-bot: Automated notification: CVE-2027-4421 detected in dependency tree (severity: HIGH). link: https://vuln.example/CVE-2027-4421. Affected packages: aws-signature-v4-js@>=1.2.0 <1.4.3 (transitive).

olivia: thanks. first q: which services consume that package? hosted api gateway, telemetry-ingest, and a small legacy cli service. hosted-api is the only public-facing one.

maria: SLA/customer-tier note — if hosted-api is impacted we have a broad customer surface. enterprise customers on Dedicated might not hit the vulnerable path, but we need confirmation. Recommend marking P0 for hosted API if confirmation of exploitable path.

ben: quick triage results from my local: telemetry-ingest bundles it but uses signed requests server->s3 only, low exposure. hosted-api uses the lib for signature verification on upload endpoints. exploitability: medium-high because attacker can craft requests to bypass some signature checks if chain triggered.

sam: blast radius estimate: hosted-api public endpoints (PLG customers + free tier) ≈ 30% of active requests. Dedicated customers behind VPC likely okay. SLA impact: if we take hosted-api down for patching, we need a maintenance window < 90s for canary, or route to fallback model.

maria: proposed schedule: 1) immediate canary hotfix on hosted-api within 24h. 2) staged rollout to 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours with health checks. 3) telemetry-ingest patch next week as low priority. Need signoff from infra for rollback playbook.

kevin: agree. also need to know if KMS keys or audit logging flows are affected — we rotate keys monthly, but if signature verification logic changes we should ensure audit logs still include raw request headers. any regressions will hamper post-incident forensics.

ben: KMS not affected — the lib only handles request signing, not key material. audit logs: add additional header dump to debug logs for the hotfix canary (short TTL retention) so we can trace attempts without increasing long-term log retention.

olivia: ops constraints: our scheduled deploy window for hosted-api is 02:00 UTC normally. can we do an emergency patch outside window? will need on-call approval and front-end owners notified.

sam: on-call (me) ok for emergency outside window if we have a tested rollback. prefer to do canary now in staging and push to canary in 2h, full emergency deploy if canary stable.

kevin: suggested action items:
- ben: prepare patch branch + changelog + backport PR to 1.4.x (if needed).
- ben: add temporary header debug log in canary only.
- olivia: notify PLG channel and set public status page draft in case we escalate.
- maria: prepare customer impact matrix (which customers on hosted-api, Dedicated, Private).
- sam: run canary deploy and monitor for 4h, then escalate.

ben: will open PR in 20m. sample check I used:
```
# find consumers in repo
yarn why aws-signature-v4-js || true
# or for go
go list -m all | grep aws-signature
```

maria: include rollout policy: if error rate > 0.5% or latency spike > 20% revert. also enable immediate audit log capture for affected endpoints for 48h.

kevin: ok locking this in. reminder: Dedicated/private customers need communication only if rollout affects them. keep the message targeted. thanks all. :thumbsup:

olivia: noted — I'll prepare the customer advisory templates in case we need them.

vuln-bot: Reminder: update the CVE ticket with mitigation steps and PR links when available.
